title: First-class van-Gogh + oil-pastel mediums + pigment-true stroke compositing
headline: Give van-Gogh + oil-pastel FIRST-CLASS distinct medium bodies riding the W12 StrokeProfile substrate: (1) kill the mediumVangogh→mediumOil passthrough — author a real body off a vangogh StrokeProfile (comma/crescent strokeShape, sparse atomic placement, full-height impasto crowns, the energy-grade as a PROFILE field not a buried uMedium==5 branch); (2) split mediumOilPastel (stroke deposition + burnish) out of mediumCrayon (DRY tooth-multiply, no sheen) — they share the SUBSTRATE, not the dispatch body; (3) move paintOver's overlap composite into OKLab on the painterly stroke mediums so complementaries mix as pigment not grey; (4) move the within-stroke streak modulation into OKLCh hue+chroma (atom-level broken color); (5) resolve the crayon strokeMode legacy peer-route — PROMOTE crayon to a first-class medium + REMOVE the strokeMode:"crayon" alias. WebGL2/GLSL mediums ONLY — the WGSL twin gains NO medium dispatch (the §4-note-14 guard holds).

The promote keeps the dry-crayon body with a live consumer (`medium:"crayon"`), so substrate-with-consumer holds; the remove strikes the legacy alias. The consumer-sweep (Cadence §2b) found three shipped demo presets (CRAYON_SUNSET/RAINBOW/OCEAN, labelled 'Pastel … creamy') + a strokeMode 'Crayon' tab option using the alias — they are RE-POINTED in the same wave (the presets to `medium:"oil-pastel"` per their creamy-pastel labels; the option moved to the medium tab) so the clean break does NOT silently no-op a consumer. Recorded default taken per Cadence §3a (the §5.3 ratify reached impl un-ratified; the orchestrator-recorded REMOVE default applied + the consumer-sweep cadence step run).

folds.finding: slice 8 F0 — the van-Gogh one-line passthrough (the headline)
folds.rootCause: AW.W4.3 reused bestOil+curvedStroke verbatim, collapsing van-Gogh into a thin uMedium==5 energy-grade switch on the oil engine. mediumVangogh has been `return mediumOil(...)` since. Real Van Gogh atomicity is NOT a length modulation — it is separable directional dabs with their OWN shape/spacing/impasto.
folds.gestaltFix: mediumVangogh is now a FIRST-CLASS body composing its OWN vangogh StrokeProfile: (a) a new comma/crescent strokeShape (type==4, asymmetric taper — a loaded round head drawn to a fine tail); (b) SPARSE atomic placement (densityBig=0.42 vs oil's 0.65 — visible inter-stroke canvas gaps); (c) the energy grade as a PROFILE FIELD (energyGrade=1.0, un-buried from bestOil — the `if (uMedium==5)` branch is gone, bestOil energy-grades off the `energyGrade` parameter); (d) full-height impasto crowns (impastoFloor=1.0 — each atomic dab catches its own glint). The bridge forces tensor orientation so the dabs queue into swirl-rows. The bestOil/curvedStroke placement substrate is REUSED through the profile, never re-authored.
folds.evidence: mediums.glsl.ts: mediumVangogh composes profileFor(MEDIUM_VANGOGH, 0) → paintStrokeMedium; the MEDIUM_VANGOGH profile case sets shapeType=4 / densityBig=0.42 / energyGrade=1.0 / impastoFloor=1.0. brush.glsl.ts: strokeShape type==4 (comma/crescent); bestOil takes a `float energyGrade` param + grades off it (the buried `if(uMedium==5)` is gone). proof:aurora-vangogh-preset (re-authored) GREEN.

folds.finding: slice 8 F1 — oil-pastel and crayon share ONE dispatch body
folds.rootCause: AW.W4.4's 'no parallel duplicate medium' precept collapsed two materially-different media (waxy oil-pastel vs dry crayon) onto one mediumCrayon dispatch body; the rework was a per-pixel tooth deposition/scumble/burnish, never a stroke.
folds.gestaltFix: Authored a DISTINCT mediumOilPastel — broad smeared directional strokes deposited via the shared brush engine off its OWN oil-pastel StrokeProfile (creamy soft hardness=0.42 so strokes blend on overlap, heavy build-up, chroma punch). mediumCrayon reverts to the DRY tooth-multiply (a tooth-relief col-multiply + a hard scumble + OKLCh broken color, NO sheen/burnish — that waxy gloss is oil-pastel's signature). aurora.frag.ts re-points uMedium==6 → mediumOilPastel; uMedium==4 keeps mediumCrayon. The two media share the SUBSTRATE (the structure-tensor orientation + tooth noise + brokenColorJitter, or the stroke cascade), NOT the dispatch body.
folds.evidence: mediums.glsl.ts: mediumOilPastel (profileFor(MEDIUM_OILPASTEL,0) → paintStrokeMedium); mediumCrayon (dry tooth-multiply, no burnish/sheen). aurora.frag.ts: uMedium==4→mediumCrayon, uMedium==6→mediumOilPastel. proof:aurora-oilpastel-medium (re-authored) GREEN.

folds.finding: slice 8 F2 — stroke OVER-compositing is linear-RGB (overlap muds to grey)
folds.rootCause: AW.W4 §10 deferred the Kubelka-Munk fold; W5 moved palette interpolation + broken-color jitter into OKLCh but left stroke OVER-compositing (paintOver's mix) in linear-RGB. The muddy-midtone defect OKLCh killed at the palette layer RE-ENTERS at the compositing layer (the trigger condition — dense atomic van-Gogh dabs overlapping — is now met).
folds.gestaltFix: paintOver composites overlapping strokes in OKLab on the painterly stroke mediums only (a paintOverOklab helper lerps L,a,b of the over-color toward the under-color via linOklab/oklabToLinearSrgb — the Ottosson matrices spliced from the shared procedural-color chunk, no new color math). Overlapping complementaries transition through a chromatic path, not grey. Gated to isPainterlyStroke (uMedium 3|5|6); the smooth pole keeps the cheap linear mix.
folds.evidence: brush.glsl.ts: paintOverOklab + isPainterlyStroke; `col = isPainterlyStroke() ? paintOverOklab(col, c, alpha) : mix(col, c, alpha)`. proof:aurora-stroke-composite (new) GREEN.
folds.disposition: ADDRESSED (OKLab; KM-as-LUT recorded for live escalation per Open-Question 1)

folds.finding: slice 8 F5 — broken color is per-CELL, not within-stroke (flat stamped swatches)
folds.rootCause: brokenColorJitter applied ONCE at the stroke cell center (one constant jittered hue for the whole stroke); the within-stroke streak modulated VALUE only, never HUE — no atom-level broken color.
folds.gestaltFix: The within-stroke streak modulation moved into OKLCh — perturbs HUE (.z) + CHROMA (.y) along alongT/crossN, seeded per-stroke off a decorrelated streak fBm (so hue ≠ a scaled value), gated to the painterly stroke mediums + uBrokenColor. A single stroke now carries a small hue gradient — broken color at the ATOM level (adjacent strokes shimmer like real impasto).
folds.evidence: brush.glsl.ts paintOver: `lch = oklabToOklch(linOklab(c)); lch.z += hueStreak * …; lch.y = max(lch.y * …); c = oklabToLinearSrgb(oklchToOklab(lch))`, gated by isPainterlyStroke() && uBrokenColor. proof:aurora-stroke-composite (new) GREEN.

folds.finding: slice 26 F5 — the crayon strokeMode legacy peer-route (a live silent special-case)
folds.rootCause: The older crayon strokeMode was kept as a peer-medium alias when the medium/strokeMode axes were reworked; neither excised nor failing. The legacy lane deferred its disposition to the aurora simplification wave; the oil-pastel/crayon split forces it here.
folds.gestaltFix: RESOLVED ONE way: PROMOTE crayon to a first-class `AuroraMedium` (uMedium==4) + REMOVE the strokeMode:"crayon" union member, the resolveMediumId/resolveStrokeModeId special-cases, and the mediums.glsl.ts legacy fall-through (clean break, no alias). The bridge forces tensor for crayon (like vangogh/oil-pastel). The consumer-sweep re-pointed the three shipped demo presets + the strokeMode tab option so the clean break does not silently no-op a consumer; the atoms-door applyTexture switch gained a `case "crayon"` (strokeAmount + canvasGrain) so a `medium:"crayon"` atom does not silently no-op the texture amount.
folds.evidence: presets.ts: AuroraMedium += crayon; StrokeMode = oil|knife|chunky (crayon removed). uniformBridge.ts: resolveMediumId is a pure identity map; STROKE_MODE_ID Record<StrokeMode>; resolveStrokeOrientId forces tensor for crayon. atoms.ts: applyTexture case "crayon". demo presets/options re-pointed. proof:aurora-oilpastel-medium step (5) GREEN.
